11.  When assessing the nutritional status of a patient with chronic kidney disease undergoing 
chronic hemodialysis, it is important to use the patient’s estimated dry weight for all 
calculations. Which of the following is the best definition of “dry weight”?
a. The weight when the patient is dehydrated
b. The weight when the patient has not drunk any fluids in 12 hours
c. The weight after the patient has received dialysis
d. The weight of the patient when no apparent edema or hypertension is present
12.  NW is a 46-year-old male with stage 4 chronic kidney disease. He weighs 200 lbs (90.9 kg), 
an ideal body weight for him, and he is not retaining fluid. A 24-hour urine collection indicated 
a loss of 2.1 grams of protein due to proteinuria, but not likely significant to add to his protein 
needs. What are his daily protein requirements?
a. 50.3 g/day
b. 56.5 g/day
c. 73 g/day
d. 121 g/day
